transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-05
Time: 15:00 EST
Duration (calendar): 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Velasquez (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (Solstice CTO), Nadia Park (Solstice Head of ML), Samir Patel (Infra)

Agenda (quick):
- Current usage & budget constraints
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs for bursty merchant queries
- Batching/caching levers and pilot scope
- Security/compliance questions (KMS, SSO)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Customer runs a commerce search/chat assistant across 1.2M monthly shoppers; primary ask is to understand cost profile for high-burst weekend traffic, options to keep latency under 250ms 95th, and how Redwood batching/caching reduces unit costs vs naive per-token billing. They want pilot pricing lanes and SOC2/network diagrams.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on a Tuesday, quick intros - I'm Maya with Redwood, Omar's my SE focused on infra and perf.
[00:12] Liam: yeah hi thanks, I'm Liam CTO at Solstice. we've got Nadia and Samir as well. Good to meet you both.
[00:18] Nadia: hey. we'll listen in mainly for cost and perf tradeoffs.
[00:22] Omar: nice to meet you. quick nit, I saw your note about weekend bursts and holiday peaks — that's actually a common pattern we design for. want to start with a quick picture of current traffic?
[00:33] Liam: sure. typical baseline is around 600 qps across the storefront helpers, but we spike to ~3k qps during big promos, sometimes longer than an hour. average prompt length is 120 tokens but some are 400-500 tokens for full context replies.
[00:50] Samir: and budget wise, finance gave us a hard stop of $40k mo for inference while we prove value.
[00:58] Maya: got it. so the main questions are: can we hit your latency targets under burst, and how do we keep per-unit cost within the 40k? also are you open to a Dedicated/reserved lane for predictable capacity?
[01:12] Liam: yeah that's the tradeoff — we want predictable latency for checkout-related prompts (SLO 95th < 250ms) but we can't blow budget. thinking maybe host some traffic hosted, keep heavy traffic on dedicated if needed?
[01:25] Nadia: one more constraint — data residency. some user PII flows through prompts, need KMS and audit logs for PCI-ish audits.
[01:33] Omar: thanks, that's helpful. mechanically, Redwood has three options: Hosted (fast to start, pay per-token, streaming), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, can isolate data), and Private (VPC/on-prem where the control plane lives in customer env). Each option changes the unit economics because of reserved capacity amortization, burst allowances, and whether you can use aggressive batching/caching.
[01:56] Liam: walk me through how batching and KV cache affect per-token? we still don't have a great intuition.
[02:05] Omar: sure. two levers: batching combines many requests onto the same GPU pass so amortized GPU work per-token goes down; prefix/KV cache means repeated context (product catalog snippets, user history prefixes) are stored and not recomputed. On hosted, we auto-batch and have shared cache across requests where appropriate. With Dedicated, you can tune batch sizes and have more predictable throughput so you can use larger batches without impacting latency for critical lanes.
[02:33] Nadia: kinda obvious Q — how much savings are we talking about? 10%? 50%?
[02:39] Omar: varies. in our retail pilots we've seen 20-60% effective token-cost savings when you combine 1) batching aligned to request patterns and 2) prefix caching. Example: if your baseline is 1.0 cost units/token without caching, a 2x effective batch with a 30% prefix reuse can push unit down 35-45%. the devil's in sequence length distribution and how many requests can be batched within your latency SLO.
[03:03] Liam: okay, sounds promising. Another thing: on peak days we have sustained 3k qps for ~90 minutes. does Hosted burst? or do we need Dedicated?
[03:13] Maya: hosted supports burst to an extent (we have burst capacity and auto-scaling), but for sustained high qps you hit economics — hosted per-token rates are higher for sustained load versus reserved Dedicated where you buy commit and pay lower unit on steady-state. For a 3k sustained we'd probably model Dedicated lanes or blended routing: checkout-critical through Dedicated, non-critical routed to hosted with SLO fallbacks.
[03:37] Samir: on Dedicated, can we pin models and versions? we need reproducible outputs for auditing.
[03:42] Omar: yes — you can pin model versions, and we support canary rollouts. Private option is available if you need the control plane inside your VPC for strict audits.
[03:51] Liam: can you explain the pricing shape — is Dedicated flat monthly plus per-token, or just flat?
[03:58] Maya: typically Dedicated involves a reserved monthly cost for capacity (GPU pool) and a lower effective per-token compute charge for usage above baseline—we'll send a sample pricing sheet. there's also burst credits and autoscale policies you can configure.
[04:12] Nadia: about encryption — we use GCP KMS and need HSM-backed keys for some merchant data. Redwood supports KMS integrations?
[04:20] Omar: yes, we integrate with KMS providers (GCP, AWS) and can support customer-managed keys. audit logs are available per-request. small note: in some Hosted plans, logs are retained for a set window unless you add extended logging retention.
[04:38] Liam: competitor question — we looked at Anthropic and doing some experiments in-house with a trimmed model. cost wise, how do you stack?
[04:46] Maya: higher level — hosting with Redwood usually beats the ops cost of self-hosting at scale because of infra, SRE, and perf tuning. Compared to Anthropic/OpenAI — raw cost per-token can be competitive, depends on model choice and whether you're using reserved capacity; we'll include direct comparisons in the workbook.
[05:02] Samir: what about latency — we need 95th 250ms. What's realistic for a 120-token prompt?
[05:09] Omar: 120 tokens on optimized runtimes can hit under 200ms 95th on dedicated GPUs with batching tuned, sometimes mid 100s. On hosted with shared noisy neighbors, you might see slightly higher tail unless you reserve capacity. Also if you have long context + retrieval, end-to-end can exceed that unless you cache retrieval results.
[05:33] Nadia: retrieval — we do a semantic search before prompt assembly. Can that be cached?
[05:38] Omar: yes, hot results can be cached; we also support prefix caching so if retrieval results are stable for short windows we can avoid re-embedding or re-including heavy context.
[05:48] Liam: ok show me an example calc — I'm a visual person.
[05:51] Maya: we'll send a workbook but briefly: take average tokens per request (prompt+response) e.g., 300 tokens. Multiply by monthly requests — convert qps to monthly calls. Apply per-token rate then apply batch factor (reduce effective tokens by X) and cache hit rate (subtract cached tokens). The workbook will show lanes: hosted baseline, dedicated reserved, private with infra ops cost.
[06:12] Samir: a little worried about unpredictable spikes causing billing surprises on hosted. is there a way to cap spending?
[06:18] Maya: yes — you can set per-key or per-route quotas and alerts; we also recommend pilot commit lanes so you get predictable reserved portions and less exposure to surprise burn.
[06:27] Nadia: what's the smallest pilot worth running? we have some dev traffic and can route 10% of checkout to a pilot.
[06:33] Omar: a 10% lane for a month with sample burst windows is enough to estimate batchability and cache-hit rates. that plus our perf logs will let us project full-run economics with +/- 10-15% accuracy.
[06:45] Liam: legal will ask about data residency and access to logs — can we get sample SOC2 artifacts?
[06:50] Maya: yes I'll attach SOC2 + network diagrams and the security whitepaper. Also an optional security review with our security engineer is doable next week.
[06:59] (brief crosstalk)
[07:05] Samir: another infra question — do you support colocated GPUs or multi-tenant? we need to avoid noisy neighbor in peak.
[07:11] Omar: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools that are tenant-isolated. Hosted is multi-tenant but we mitigate noisy neighbor with scheduling and prioritization; for critical low-tail latency, Dedicated or Private is safer.
[07:27] Nadia: in the price workbook, can you include sensitivity to cache hit rates? i.e., what if cache is only 10% vs 40%?
[07:33] Maya: absolutely — we'll provide scenarios.
[07:36] Liam: how about fallback policies — e.g., if Dedicated saturated, do you fallback to hosted?
[07:41] Omar: yes, routing policies can failover to hosted-compatible model variants. You can set priority rules: prefer dedicated, then hosted, with graceful degradation and short-circuit responses for non-critical calls.
[07:55] Samir: what about quantization — we tried 8-bit internally and saw latency improvements but quality hits. Can Redwood recommend quantization profiles?
[08:03] Omar: our Optimize tooling will recommend quantization and model variants per workload. For many e-com generative tasks, 4/8-bit quantization with a calibrated eval set keeps quality high. We'll run an eval on a small set.
[08:16] Nadia: evaluation — we need to measure hallucination on checkout dialogs. Are there integrated evals or do we need to supply test sets?
[08:23] Maya: both. we can run Redwood verify on your test set; if you want to start, send a representative prompt set and we'll return quality and perf metrics.
[08:33] Liam: timeline — finance wants to sign pilot budget in two weeks. can you get a pilot quote by Jan 7?
[08:40] Maya: yes we'll prioritize that. Omar will do perf estimates and I'll assemble pilot pricing lanes.
[08:44] Liam: perfect.
[08:47] (speaker labeled as Speaker 1, transcription glitch) Speaker 1: uh we have a question about SAML and SSO, sorry crosstalk
[08:52] Maya: yes we support SAML/SSO integrations and RBAC. will include the integration guide link.
[08:58] Samir: curious about tokenization and counting — do we count tokens before or after detokenization stuff? sometimes our internal count differs from vendor count.
[09:06] Omar: good point — token counting differs by tokenizer. we provide tooling to run your sample prompts to show vendor token counts; main note is to standardize on the same tokenizer in the workbook.
[09:16] Nadia: what about long-term cost optimizations — is there a recommended strategy month 1 versus month 6?
[09:22] Omar: yes — month 1 pilot focuses on measurement and conservative caching; month 2-3 tune batching and routing; month 4+ you lock in reserved lanes for predictable baseline and keep hosted for bursts, plus active quantization and model pruning if quality allows.
[09:36] Liam: ok good. can you flag any hard blockers we should be aware of?
[09:40] Maya: main blockers: data residency & SOC2 acceptability, budget alignment for Dedicated reserve, and availability windows for pilot (need a week with representative bursts).
[09:50] Samir: on the SOC2 point, can we get redaction or partial logs for PII?
[09:55] Omar: yes, we can redact or restrict access; audit logs remain but you can limit exposure and use customer-managed keys to encrypt sensitive blobs.
[10:05] Nadia: one small ops ask — can you instrument token-level cost per route in the console? we want per-route dashboards.
[10:11] Maya: console has per-route token cost breakdown and latency histograms; we can also add custom tags for your teams.
[10:18] (brief pause)
[10:22] Liam: solid. I'm comfortable moving forward with a pilot ask, but need the workbook and security docs. We'll aim to commit pilot funding pending the numbers.
[10:32] Maya: great - recap of next steps: 1) Maya send pricing workbook, SOC2 and network diagram, console screenshots; 2) Omar run perf estimate for 3k spikes and 2k baseline with batching assumptions; 3) schedule pilot scope call with Nadia and team.
[10:47] Liam: and legal will want a short security review — put that in as optional next step.
[10:52] Maya: will do. thanks everyone. we'll follow up by Jan 7 with materials.
[10:58] (meeting ends)
